lead_headline: One ASA Sushi opening lead in LoHi — tracker mostly quiet on Monday despite 287 active leads still in pipeline

restaurant.blurb: Single opening lead today: ASA Sushi prepping second location in LoHi at 1535 Central St. Active pipeline steady at 287 leads (156 openings, 131 closures).

liquor.blurb: The freeze breaks. After 45 days dormant, Colorado's liquor licensing pipeline roared back to life Monday with 63 genuine new applications — the first real activity since late May. Notable filings: Mother Other (vegan restaurant at 675 S Broadway), Olive & Finch expanding to Golden Triangle at 1140 N Bannock, Tapster Tasting Room (self-pour concept at 3200 N Tejon in LoHi), and Spitz Mediterranean in RiNo. Hotel & Restaurant licenses dominate (19), followed by Taverns (8), Fermented Malt Beverage (7). Plus 173 status changes — scores of previously delinquent licenses suddenly resolving to active or expired. The state's six-week administrative blackout ends without explanation. Pipeline now shows 331 applications in 7-day window vs. zero last Monday. Whether this represents genuine new investment or bureaucratic catch-up remains unclear, but Denver hospitality filings are officially moving again.

reputation.blurb: 3 mentions yesterday — Monday pickup after Saturday's single-citation lull. Week now at 78 citations across 18 sources, up 10% from last week's 71 and marking the highest 7-day total since late June. Instagram leads with 19 (IMAC building demolition post viral), followed by Denver Post (17), Facebook (14), Reddit (10). Google News RSS captured 77 of 78 (99% efficiency). Notable recent pickups: Weld County correctional facility redevelopment coverage, Daily Mail running Denver socialite angle, multiple IMAC tower stories gaining traction on social. Three-week upward trend now clear: 72 → 75 → 78, suggesting post-holiday momentum building into mid-summer. Source diversity expanding — 18 unique outlets vs. 16 last week.

subscriptions.blurb: Net −1 yesterday (0 new, 1 canceled) — eleventh consecutive day without positive growth. MTD now slides negative to −4 (−0.3/day), while 90-day cumulative holds at +108. The July collapse accelerates: eleven straight days underwater crushes the +1.1/day YTD baseline. Since July 1, the operation netted just 17 new subscribers while bleeding 34 cancellations — a −17 combined deficit worse than any comparable fortnight on record. Past two weeks show zero acquisition momentum: 7-day net sits at −17 (17 new, 34 canceled) vs. prior week's +22 (51 new, 29 canceled). The churn ratio inverted catastrophically — cancellations now running 2:1 against new sign-ups. If July's pattern holds through month-end, it'll mark the first negative monthly net since tracking began. No recovery signal visible.
